title: node-tiling-and-latency-gardening-weekly-log-mar-2026
content:
Weekly (Mar 9–11) — Node tiling & latency gardening

Context: ongoing VPC/onprem installs across three customers (Atria Health, EmberDocs, Greybox Analytics). This note captures the standup highlights, field observations, emergent customer blockers, and a set of small experiments that surfaced unusual tail-latency behavior on small node counts. Informal — notes-to-self style; shareable with install squad and SEs.

TL;DR
- Two installs green (Atria day+1 warmback), one customer (Greybox) hit persistent KV cache mismatch causing 95th pct spikes.
- Network MTU mismatches and SMB mount flakiness were root-cause for two transient failures; applied conservative MTU and mount-timeout defaults.
- Experiment: node-tiling (breaking a 4-GPU farm into 2x2 logical pools) reduced tail latency on short queries by ~18% in lab (see perf snapshots linked).
- Open action: PD-4123 — validate KV cache eviction resume semantics on quantized models (owner: Marcus).

Standup snippets (concise):
- Priya: Atria recovered; node-tiling trial scheduled Thu; added additional logging to KV path.
- Lena: EmberDocs had slow image ingest to NFS during profiling — workaround: direct S3 pull, patching install script to avoid CIFS in pod.
- Marcus: Greybox root cause suspected KV serialization mismatch after hot-reload; isolation test in sandbox failed to repro; raised PD-4123.
- Jiayi: Networking team patched firewall rule ordering; still seeing 10–20ms variance on internal hops.

Customer-specific notes
- Atria Health (on-prem, small cluster, 3 nodes):
  - Symptom: occasional request stalls ~400–600ms on short prompt completions; frequency dropped after applying MTU 1458 and disabling LRO on NIC.
  - What we changed: bumped agent loglevel for cache miss path, enabled periodic KV checksum reporting to controller.
  - Next: follow up Thursday after 48h warmback; if persists, plan full dump of KV metrics for model stage.
  - Contact: SE Zoe Park.

- EmberDocs (VPC hosted in customer account):
  - Symptom: NFS/CIFS mount churn when concurrent ingest > 60MB/s; leads to pod restarts.
  - Workaround: changed install flow to stage files directly to S3 then sync into pods via initContainer; longer-term: recommend S3-backed volume or provisionded NAS with stable mount options.
  - Owner for followup: Lena (SE) + Infra (storage).

- Greybox Analytics (edge onprem testbed):
  - Symptom: consistent 95th pct jump to ~1.2s under RBAC hot-reload.
  - Hypothesis: KV cache eviction + serialization mismatch on quantized layers when fallback model variant is activated.
  - Immediate action: rollback hot-reload flag for canary traffic and run isolation harness.
  - Jira: PD-4123 tracking.

Field troubleshooting and observations
- MTU/LRO: Two separate installs showed path MTU anomalies due to intermediary load-balancer doing jumbo translation. Setting MTU to 1458 and disabling LRO on host NICs eliminated packet fragmentation and reduced reordering microbursts. Documenting this in the install checklist.
- SMB/CIFS instability: Several customer environments still prefer CIFS-mounted stores for legacy reasons. CIFS timeouts cause long stall cycles inside sidecars. Short-term: add timeout=30,nounix to mount options in the install script. Mid-term: advise S3 or NFSv4 where possible.
- Node-tiling experiment: In a lab recreate with 4xA100 (single farm) we tried logical tiling into 2 pools of 2 GPUs each with isolated scheduler queues. Observation: small prompt workloads (<=128 tokens) see lower tail latency because batching pressure is better isolated and KV cache locality improves per-pool. Caveat: throughput for large-batch workloads fell ~4% — need to drive policy to choose tiling by workload signature.

Runbook & checklist deltas (proposed)
- Add MTU/LRO verification step to day-zero checklist with a recommended default (MTU 1458) and a short test script (ping with DF + throughput sanity).
- Add a note in the NFS/SMB section: "If customer persists with CIFS, enable mount option timeout=30 and capture mount logs daily for first 72h."
- KV checksum daily probe: add to controller health probes; report last-checksum and mismatch count.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Marcus: PD-4123 — reproduce KV serialization mismatch in sandbox with quantized-model variant (ETA: 2026-03-13).
- Lena: Push EmberDocs install script patch to staging and run 3-replica soak (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Jiayi: Add MTU/LRO test to preflight script and PR to repo (PR #982) (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Priya: Collate daily KV checksum metrics for Atria and share with model-team for correlation (ETA: 2026-03-14).

Unresolved questions / risks
- Does node-tiling generalize to multi-tenant Dedicated pools? If we tile aggressively we risk starving large-batch customers — need simulation across mixed workloads.
- KV eviction semantics under quantized kernels are not well covered in current test harness; we may need an integration-level fuzzing job.
- Customer-run firewalls sometimes reorder packets during NAT port translation leading to subtle TCP reordering; is there a kernel-level tuning that’s safe to recommend at scale?

Notes to self (quick):
- Capture a short demo video of node-tiling latency diff for internal docs.
- Ask model infra about adding a correlation key between model stage and KV checksum for quicker triage.
- Revisit canary rollout policy for hot-reloads — add a forced idle-check period after any KV schema change.

Meeting cadence & next sync
- Daily light standup 10:15 PT (15 min) while installs active.
- Deep triage session Friday 11:00 PT (30–45 min) to review PD-4123 findings and node-tiling perf traces.

Attachments / links (quick):
- perf-snapshots: internal perf-dashboard link (Confluence attached)
- install scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/install-scripts/tree/mtu-check (see PR #45)

If you’re reading this and have run into similar CIFS flakiness or MTU-induced fragmentation, ping #install-field and drop the packet capture (pcap).

-- Priya
